To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the ACL Anthology corpus was manually annotated for semantic relations; (b) the semantic relations were defined based on an empirical study of the text sequences between concepts; (c) 18 specific relations were defined, plus 3 generic relations; (d) the semantic relations are explicit and not inferred; (e) the semantic relations can be applied to any corpus, and are not specific to the ACL Anthology;

(1) the ACL Anthology corpus is a good candidate for the annotation of scientific texts; (2) concepts can be identified and annotated fully-automatically; (3) a corpus-based typology of semantic relation types can be defined, based on the most frequent sequences of concepts in sentences.
(1) concepts can be extracted automatically from scientific texts, and (2) semantic relations can also be extracted automatically from these texts, using a corpus-based approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic extraction of information from scientific corpora.
the automatic annotation of scientific texts with concepts and relations, and the development of a corpus for the evaluation of semantic relation classification techniques.
the automatic annotation of scientific literature with concepts and semantic relations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ACL Anthology is a very good corpus, and that it has been annotated in a good manner.
the ACL Anthology corpus is the most important corpus in the field of computational linguistics.

this paper describes a process that can be applied to any corpus of scientific papers, and that it can be used to create an annotated corpus of scientific literature, with concepts and explicit semantic relations, for the automatic analysis of scientific literature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a corpus annotation methodology, which is based on a combination between a typology of semantic relation and an ontology-based approach to the identification and annotation of concepts.
we have created a corpus annotated with concepts and explicit semantic relations, which could be used to train or evaluate automatic semantic relation classification systems.
the annotation of scientific corpora with semantic information can be performed in an automatic way, with a good level of reliability, and with a relatively small effort.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to create an annotated scientific corpus that is large enough to train a statistical semantic relation classifier, but still small enough to be manually annotated.
it is possible to create a corpus annotated for semantic relations in a fully automatic way, without the need for a human expert to be involved in the annotation process.

it is possible to create a large corpus of scientific articles with concepts annotated and semantic relations identified automatically, and to use it as a training corpus for the evaluation of automatic semantic relation classifiers.
